title: What would you build if trust stopped being the bottleneck?
subtitle: Three rival Alzheimer's programmes. Three dead candidates. Nothing shared.
narration: What would you build if trust stopped being the bottleneck? Three rival Alzheimer's labs each killed a drug candidate last year. Will they tell each other? No way. Whoever runs the shared server could read it, and whoever shares first gets scooped. So the same failures get funded again. And again.
caption: Rival labs repeat each other's failures, because nobody can share safely.

title: Every shared platform has a landlord
subtitle:
The host can read everything.
One admin can let anyone in, or peek early.
narration: Here's the catch. It's not the science. It's the landlord. Every shared platform has one. The host can read everything you upload. And a single admin can let anyone in, or sneak an early peek.
caption: Every shared platform has a landlord who can read it and let anyone in.

title: Treaty Room
subtitle:
A sealed research room that no one owns.
Deposits are encrypted in each researcher's browser, to the room.
The room is sealed, even to the depositors.
narration: So we built Treaty Room. A sealed research room that nobody owns. Not even us. Your deposit is encrypted right in your own browser, locked to the room itself. And once it's in? The room stays sealed. Even to the people who put it there.
caption: Encrypted in the browser. Sealed in the room, even to depositors.

title: Our database holds only ciphertext
subtitle:
Stolen data can't be opened.
Ask the Tide network for the key without a treaty, and it refuses.
narration: Now look at what we, the host, actually see. Ciphertext. That's it. Steal our whole database, and you've got nothing you can open. Ask the Tide network for the key? Refused. Flat out.
caption: The host holds only ciphertext. Tide refuses to decrypt it.

title: An admin grants himself early access
subtitle:
The change is drafted, then stalls at 1 of 2 approvals.
Nothing opens.
narration: But what about an inside job? Say a steward with admin rights grants himself early access. On an ordinary system? Game over. Here, his change stalls at one of two approvals. And nothing opens.
caption: A rogue admin stalls at 1 of 2 approvals. Nothing opens.

title: Two of three institutions co-sign
subtitle:
Each signs inside its own Tide enclave.
At quorum, the room opens for every member at once.
narration: So how does anyone get in? By treaty. Two of the three institutions co-sign, each inside its own Tide enclave. The moment they hit quorum, the room opens for every member at once. Nobody gets a head start.
caption: 2 of 3 institutions co-sign, and the room opens for everyone at once.

title: Not a checkbox. A quorum.
subtitle:
Ordinary login: every rule is an admin checkbox and a promise.
TideCloak: the key never exists whole.
Tide's nodes check membership on every request.
Access changes only through a quorum of enclave signatures.
narration: Why TideCloak? With an ordinary login, every rule is an admin checkbox. And a promise. With TideCloak, the key never exists in one piece. Tide's nodes check membership on every single request. And access only changes with a quorum of enclave signatures. No single party holds the key.
caption: Not a checkbox. A quorum: no single party holds the key.

title: We built this platform, and we can't read it or open it alone.
subtitle: We built it, and we can't read it or open it alone.
narration: We built it. And we can't read it, or open it, alone. That's Treaty Room, from Team Sunway PowerRanger. Every bit of data in this demo is synthetic.
